title: Implement pluggable preflight check framework for Private upgrades
author: Bruno Silva
description: Summary: This PR introduces a pluggable preflight check framework in the Private installer. The framework standardizes check execution, result reporting, severity levels, and remediation pointers so upgrades are safer-by-default and failures are actionable for operators. Context: Part of the “Private upgrade + rollback mechanism” effort. This PR focuses on the framework + CLI surface for preflight runs; follow-up PRs will add/expand the actual checks (cluster health, storage, RBAC/SSO reachability, artifact availability, etc.). Goals: (1) Make prechecks composable (registerable plugins) and deterministic, (2) Provide consistent UX for operators and Support, (3) Establish blocking vs warning semantics that can be used by upgrade plan generation and change-management gating. Design notes: Checks are registered by ID and grouped into named phases (environment, control-plane, data-plane, artifacts). Each check returns a CheckResult with: status (PASS/WARN/FAIL/SKIP), severity (BLOCKER/WARNING/INFO), a short summary, optional details, and remediation pointers (human-readable steps + optional doc links). The runner supports timeouts per-check, a global deadline, and produces both console output and a JSON artifact suitable for audit/support bundles. CLI: Adds `redwood-private preflight run` (alias wired for upgrade flows in subsequent PRs). Supports `--format=table|json`, `--output <path>`, `--fail-on-warning` (default false), `--include`/`--exclude` (by check ID or group), and `--timeout` controls. Output example (json): `{ "run_id": "pf_...", "installer_version": "0.19.0", "target_version": "private-1.42.0", "results": [ ... ], "summary": { "blockers": 0, "warnings": 2 } }` (full schema in `docs/preflight-result-schema.md`). Implementation details: - New package `internal/preflight/` with: `registry` (check registration + metadata), `runner` (execution + concurrency limits), and `report` (renderers: table/json). - Standardized error taxonomy for checks to map common failures into remediation hints (e.g., kube auth failure vs API server unreachable vs RBAC forbidden). - Basic built-in checks included as scaffolding/examples: Kubernetes API reachability, namespace write access, and installer artifact writeability (output dir). These are intentionally minimal; real upgrade checks land in ENG-4829 follow-ups. - Adds a persistent “last preflight” record under the installer state dir to be consumed by the upgrade planner (plan generator PR) and support bundles. - Logging: all checks emit structured logs with `check_id`, `severity`, and `status` fields; runner emits a single summary line for easy grep during on-call. Operator UX: Table output uses stable ordering and explicitly labels “BLOCKING” items; remediation text is capped in the table view with a `--verbose` option to print full remediation steps. Testing: Unit tests cover registration, include/exclude filtering, timeout handling, renderer output stability, and JSON schema validation. Integration test spins up a kind cluster and validates kube reachability + RBAC check behavior under simulated restricted RBAC. Checklist: - [x] Framework + registry + runner - [x] JSON + table renderers - [x] Minimal built-in checks as examples - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Docs: result schema + CLI usage - [ ] Add full precheck inventory (follow-up PRs under ENG-4829) Notes for reviewers: Please focus on (a) severity semantics (BLOCKER/WARNING/INFO) and defaults, (b) output stability (Support will consume this), and (c) security concerns around logging potentially sensitive info in remediation/details. Release notes: Adds new `preflight run` command and machine-readable preflight output artifact to support upgrade gating and troubleshooting.
commits: preflight: add check registry + metadata model
preflight: implement runner with timeouts and include/exclude filters
cli: add `preflight run` command with table/json output
report: add table renderer and JSON schema validation tests
tests: kind-based integration test for kube reachability + RBAC denial
docs: document preflight result schema and operator-facing CLI usage
review_conversation: Irene Choi: The framework looks good. One concern: remediation messages should never echo kubeconfig contents or full endpoint URLs for private clusters. Can we sanitize/trim? Bruno Silva: Good call. I updated the kube reachability check to log only hostnames (no tokens/paths) and redacted query strings; also added a `SafeDetails()` helper that defaults to redaction for error types we control.

Sean Gallagher: For gating, we need deterministic semantics: FAIL+BLOCKER must abort upgrade, WARN+BLOCKER should probably also abort by default. What’s the default behavior? Bruno Silva: Default is: any FAIL+BLOCKER returns non-zero exit code. WARN never fails unless `--fail-on-warning` is set. Severity is orthogonal; WARN+BLOCKER is allowed but we should avoid generating that combination in real checks. I added a validation in the registry to reject WARN+BLOCKER for now so we don’t create ambiguous gating behavior.

Kenji Nakamura: Table output truncation is helpful, but the operator needs a copy/paste remediation. Suggest printing remediation in full when there are blockers even without `--verbose`. Bruno Silva: Agreed. Updated renderer: if there is any blocking result, we append a “Remediation details” section with full steps for those checks. Non-blocking warnings remain truncated unless `--verbose`.

Marcus Lin: Please ensure we don’t allow check plugins to execute arbitrary shells by default. Are checks just Go functions in-process? Bruno Silva: Yes—checks are compiled into the installer binary and are registered at init time. No dynamic loading, no shell execution helpers added here. I also added a note in docs that checks must not run `kubectl`/shell and should use client-go to avoid leaking env state.

Sahana Iyer: Integration test flaked once on CI due to kind API server readiness. Can we add a wait/retry with bounded timeout? Bruno Silva: Added a readiness wait with exponential backoff (max 60s) before running the kube reachability check, and pinned kind node image to the version we use in other installer tests.
